title: Stock Futures Tick Up as Dow Endures Third Consecutive Losing Week – Live Updates】
body:
Wall Street’s major indices closed a turbulent week on a downbeat note, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipping for the third consecutive session, while futures for the broader market nudged higher on Sunday night, hinting at a tentative rebound ahead of the new trading week. The S&P 500 futures rose 0.23 % and Nasdaq‑100 futures climbed 0.27 % in after‑hours trading, suggesting investors are cautiously optimistic despite the recent string of losses.

The Dow’s slide marked its third straight weekly decline, extending a pattern not seen since the early months of the pandemic. Over the past five trading days, the blue‑chip index shed roughly 1.1 % after a volatile start to the month that saw technology stocks swing sharply on earnings reports and macro‑economic data. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite each posted modest gains for the week, with the tech‑heavy Nasdaq edging up 0.4 % while the broader S&P 500 eked out a 0.2 % rise. The divergent performance underscores the market’s split between defensive, dividend‑paying industrials and growth‑oriented technology firms that remain sensitive to interest‑rate expectations.

A key driver of the week’s mixed results was the Federal Reserve’s latest policy stance. Although the central bank held rates steady, officials reiterated that further tightening remains possible if inflation does not continue its gradual decline. That message kept bond yields elevated, with the 10‑year Treasury yield hovering near 4.6 %, a level that typically pressures high‑valuation tech stocks. Yet, the same higher yields have benefitted financials and energy companies, which contributed to the Dow’s resilience despite its overall dip. Analysts note that investors are now weighing the Fed’s “higher‑for‑longer” narrative against signs that core inflation is finally edging lower, creating a delicate balancing act for equity markets.

Corporate earnings also played a pivotal role. Several heavyweight tech firms, including a leading cloud‑services provider and a major semiconductor designer, reported results that beat expectations, fueling optimism for the Nasdaq‑100 futures. However, a handful of consumer‑discretionary names posted weaker‑than‑expected sales, reflecting lingering concerns about disposable income as households grapple with higher living costs. The earnings calendar for the coming week features a cluster of reports from industrial manufacturers and retail giants, which could either reinforce the tentative bounce indicated by futures or reignite the bearish momentum that has plagued the Dow.

Global developments added another layer of uncertainty. In Europe, the eurozone’s growth outlook was downgraded amid persistent supply‑chain bottlenecks, while in Asia, China’s manufacturing PMI slipped below the expansion threshold, prompting worries about a slowdown in the world’s second‑largest economy. These external pressures have kept investors on the defensive, prompting a modest shift toward safer assets such as U.S. Treasuries and gold. Yet, the modest rise in futures suggests that market participants are still seeking opportunities in equities, especially in sectors that could benefit from a potential easing of monetary policy later in the year.

Looking ahead, the market’s direction will likely hinge on a confluence of factors: the Federal Reserve’s next policy move, the upcoming wave of earnings reports, and any fresh geopolitical or economic data that could sway sentiment. If inflation continues its gradual decline and earnings beat expectations, the modest gains in futures could translate into a stronger opening for the equity markets on Monday. Conversely, any hint of renewed inflationary pressure or a disappointing earnings slate could pull the indices back into negative territory, extending the Dow’s losing streak. Investors will be watching closely for clues that could either solidify a tentative recovery or deepen the current market uncertainty.
